What is the difference between an iterable and an iterator?

Supplied answer
An iterable is anything you can loop over (list, tuple, string, dict) - it implements __iter__(). An iterator is
the object that actually does the walking - it implements both __iter__() and __next__() and raises
StopIteration when it is finished. iter(my_list) turns an iterable into an iterator.
